attacks.claim: The agreed invariant is that devices must always be able to return to the previous firmware. The only path back for a unit that boots 4.8 but loses OTA reachability is a 4.7 push over the same OTA path, and 4.8 changes Wi-Fi reconnect behaviour. Auto-revert covers only boot failure and self-test failure, so an update client or connectivity regression can strand units with no delivered revert.
attacks.evidence: 'Revert: push 4.7 to updated units through the same OTA path' and 'Wi-Fi reconnect after router reboot now < 60 s'; ABSENT: a bootloader-level or local revert trigger for units that cannot reach the OTA service after 4.8.

attacks.claim: Away Assist can set Away during occupied home periods when occupants are stationary for 2 h, for example sleeping, reading or napping, because the sensor is motion-based. This can cut heating for people who are home. QA tested only the mocked no-motion-to-Away transition, not false Away from stationary occupants.
attacks.evidence: 'sets Away mode after 2 h with no motion during scheduled "home" periods'; QA: 'on → Away after 2 h no motion, back on motion' with ABSENT: sensitivity or stationary-occupant validation and no false-Away metric in Monitoring.

attacks.claim: A user's 8-period schedule is destroyed without notice on a 4.7 edit, because the cloud discards the v2 copy. Re-upgrading then yields only the 4-period v1 schedule. This is user data loss presented as housekeeping.
attacks.evidence: 'When a unit on 4.7 edits its schedule, the cloud discards the stale v2 copy, so a later re-upgrade starts from the current v1 schedule.'

attacks.claim: HIL coverage excludes C-wire power-stealing installs, a common field configuration. The install holds relays open for about 90 s and runs the Wi-Fi radio, which can brown out power-stealing thermostats during OTA. This risk is untested.
attacks.evidence: HIL: 'conventional 1H/1C, 2-stage, heat pump + aux, no C-wire power stealing'; 'During the ~90 s install, relays are held open (off).'

attacks.claim: The freeze and heat protection guarantee is overstated and untested at the boundary. Relays are off for about 90 s regardless of temperature, and repeated boot-revert cycles have no bounded total off time. The only deferral test was at 5 °C, with nothing at the 7 °C or 32 °C thresholds.
attacks.evidence: 'so freeze/heat protection is never interrupted'; QA: 'Temperature deferral at 5 °C chamber test'; ABSENT: total relay-off bound across 3 failed boots plus revert install.

attacks.claim: Stage gates are statistically meaningless at stage 1 and their baselines are undefined. At 6,100 units for 3 days, a 0.05% boot-revert threshold is about 3 units, and 'not above baseline' for rare HVAC faults has no defined test, so the gate can pass on noise or by default.
attacks.evidence: 'boot-revert rate < 0.05%, HVAC fault telemetry not above 4.7 baseline, support contacts per 1k units not above baseline'; ABSENT: sample-size, confidence or significance criteria.

attacks.claim: The 6% runtime claim is published, but the artifact does not state whether the 412-home trial used a control group, which firmware and Away Assist configuration were tested, or that the causal claim is supported. Legal review is cited but not the design.
attacks.evidence: 'In our 2025-26 field trial of 412 homes, Away Assist cut heating runtime by a median of 6%.'

attacks.claim: Canadian privacy-notice and consent-screen French versions are not confirmed. Only release notes and app strings are stated as French, and the revised privacy notice section 3 is not.
attacks.evidence: 'Privacy notice section 3 updated (legal review LGL-4471)'; ABSENT: French privacy notice and French Away Assist consent text.

attacks.claim: Cloud-stored Home/Away occupancy history linked to the account reveals presence and absence patterns for 7 days, and a rollback silently deletes it. Users are not told that rollback deletes their history.
attacks.evidence: 'Home/Away state ... kept 7 days'; 'Revert ... Away Assist turns off (Home/Away history is deleted).'

attacks.claim: Monitoring pages on boot reverts at 0.1% but the stage gate uses 0.05%, and it has no paging for self-test failure spikes or false-Away events. Alerting and thresholds are inconsistent.
attacks.evidence: 'Pages firmware on-call if boot reverts exceed 0.1%'; gate: 'boot-revert rate < 0.05%'.

attacks.claim: QA coverage gaps: the self-test failure revert path is untested (only failed-boot injection), the relay soak is 72 h, and the employee beta firmware version is not stated.
attacks.evidence: 'Failed-boot injection → auto revert'; 'Pass over 72 h'; 'Employee beta: 1,140 homes for 3 weeks'.

attacks.claim: The 'Some schedule changes were simplified' message has an unspecified trigger and timing. It may not appear after a 4.7 edit that discards v2, and the v1 selection heuristic can silently drop overnight setbacks.
attacks.evidence: 'The app shows "Some schedule changes were simplified" if v2 had more than 4 periods.'

attacks.claim: OTA delivery and rollback depend on a single CDN contract and a single OTA service, with no stated fallback or exit path.
attacks.evidence: 'OTA egress ... via existing CDN contract'; 'the production OTA service'.

attacks.claim: Rollback doubles egress and load on the same OTA and CDN path, and the artifact gives no peak-concurrency or check-in behaviour for 612k units.
attacks.evidence: '2.4 MB image × 612k units ≈ 1.5 TB'; ABSENT: peak concurrency and rollback egress estimate.

attacks.claim: No finding beyond egress sizing: the 1.5 TB figure excludes rollback and retry traffic, and the +0.4% telemetry projection has no stated basis.
attacks.evidence: 'projected +0.4% on telemetry ingest'.

attacks.claim: NO FINDING on signature and boot verification. Note that the anti-rollback counter is intentionally not incremented, so future security fixes must remember to increment it.
attacks.evidence: '4.8 does not increment the secure-boot anti-rollback counter'.

attacks.claim: NO FINDING: VoiceOver, TalkBack and 200% text were tested on the editor and Away Assist screens.
attacks.evidence: 'App 9.3 schedule editor and Away Assist screens with VoiceOver, TalkBack, 200% text: Pass'.

attacks.claim: NO FINDING: Away Assist is off by default and the rollout is staged.
attacks.evidence: 'Away Assist is off for every user until they turn it on.'

attacks.claim: NO FINDING: postpone and deferral behaviour is defined.
attacks.evidence: 'Users can postpone an update up to 14 days from the app.'

attacks.claim: Dual-writing v1 and v2 schedules on every edit doubles schedule logic and test surface across 4.7, 4.8 and app 9.2/9.3.
attacks.evidence: 'It also writes a v1 schedule (4 periods) on every edit'.

attacks.claim: NO FINDING: the energy claim is hedged and the 'up to' figures are excluded.
attacks.evidence: 'No "up to" figures are used anywhere.'
